{"action":"shell","command":"python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='/testbed/specs/001-transactions/spec.md'
s=open(p).read()
anchor='''- **FR-021** (R06): Returned values MUST remain detached across repeated
  `get`s and `put`s, including nested lists and dicts; no returned object
  (or object nested within one) may alias the stored value or any other
  returned object.
'''
assert anchor in s
new=anchor+'''- **FR-022** (R07): The constructor MUST accept `timer=None`; when `timer`
  is `None` the standard monotonic clock is used, otherwise the supplied
  callable is the sole source of time for expiry decisions.
- **FR-023** (R07): `put` MUST accept `ttl=None`, meaning no expiration; a
  finite nonnegative `int`/`float` (excluding `bool`) MUST set the entry's
  absolute expiry to `timer() + ttl` at insertion time.
- **FR-024** (R07): An invalid TTL (negative number, `bool`, non-numeric,
  non-finite) MUST raise `ValueError` BEFORE any mutation (no insert, no
  replace, no recency or expiry change).
- **FR-025** (R07): A `ttl=0` entry MUST be immediately expired (unobservable
  via `get`, `len`, or invalidation), and an entry MUST be treated as expired
  at the exact boundary `timer() == timer_at_put + ttl` (inclusive
  comparison); it is live just before that instant.
- **FR-026** (R08): Expired entries MUST be removed before `get`, `put`,
  `len`, `resize`, and invalidation, and the purge MUST NOT change the
  relative recency of surviving entries.
- **FR-027** (R08): Overwriting an entry MUST replace its prior expiry
  (`ttl=None` clears the expiry; a finite TTL sets a fresh absolute expiry
  from the current `timer()`); tag invalidation MUST count only live
  (unexpired) entries; a `get` for a missing or expired key MUST raise
  `KeyError`.
- **FR-028** (R08): Existing callers that never pass `timer` or `ttl` MUST
  retain exactly the pre-milestone-3 behavior (entries never expire).
'''
s=s.replace(anchor,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok FR-022..FR-028 added')
PYEOF"}
